newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope makes fresh appeal for central Africa.
newsitem.headline: Pope makes fresh appeal for central Africa.

text.p: Pope John Paul made his second appeal in as many days on Thursday for an end to violence in Zaire, where one of his bishops was killed two days ago.
The 76-year-old Pontiff made his appeal in a telegram of condolences over the death of Roman Catholic Archbishop Christophe Munzihirwa Mwene Ngabo of Bukavu.

"I beg the Lord to touch the hearts of men so that the guns are finally silenced and that feelings of hate disappear and give way to the search for peace and justice for all," the Pope said in a telegram to the head of Zaire's bishops conference.
The Pope said the bishop, who was killed in a military attack on the eastern Zairean city on Tuesday, had "given his life while sharing the trials of the people entrusted to him".
Church sources in Rome said they believed that Munzihirwa, a Zairean Jesuit, had been killed in an ambush.
Bukavu, the capital of Zaire's South Kivu province, has been under attack from ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels and Zairean troops have been on a looting spree in recent days.
On Wednesday, before news of the bishop's death reached Rome, the Pope made an impassioned plea for the world to help end the "interminable tragedy" of central Africa.
Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro sent the Pope a letter of condolences earlier on Thursday.

"Such an inhuman act is all the more vile and execrable since it took the life of a pastor of souls, involved with humility and sacrifice in his mission of brotherhood and love in a country devastated by violence and hatred," he said.
